content.text:
I wrote the migrated file to `out/module.ts`. It type-checks, but I couldn't compare it against the original because lodash isn't installed here. `src/module.ts` fails to build and to type-check, so there is no baseline size.

```ts
import { pick, sumBy } from 'es-toolkit';
import { toNumber } from 'es-toolkit/compat';
// interfaces unchanged
publicFields → pick(row, ['id', 'name'])
totalAge     → sumBy(rows, (row) => row.age)
parseAmount  → toNumber(text)
```

`npm run size -- out/module.ts` reports 267 bytes (min+gzip) and 101 bytes of own code.

| lodash | es-toolkit | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `pick` | `es-toolkit` `pick` | Same call shape. |
| `sumBy(rows, 'age')` | `es-toolkit` `sumBy` | The strict version only takes a function, so I added a small adapter, `(row) => row.age`. An empty array still gives 0. |
| `toNumber` | `es-toolkit/compat` `toNumber` | Strict `es-toolkit` has no `toNumber`. I used the compat one because it follows lodash's string handling (trimming, `0b`/`0o`/`0x` prefixes, bad signed hex giving `NaN`). `Number(text)` would be close, but it isn't a library function, so I didn't use it. |

I didn't run any equality tests against the original, so I haven't checked that results match for the input range.

I did not check the 267 bytes against the smallest size reachable. `toNumber` is the only function pulled from compat. I kept it because no strict es-toolkit function preserves its behaviour.
